source.title: Overfitting, regularisation and condition estimation in regression

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses overfitting and regularisation and gives regression examples, but it does not measure test error or test any of the listed double-descent versions.
record.gate_note: The examples report whether regression curves overfit as polynomial degree or basis count changes, but they do not report test error, epoch-wise error, or error as sample size changes. These overfitting observations are recorded as findings that fit none of the listed versions. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The paper studies when ridge (Tikhonov) regularisation should be applied to least-squares regression, using effective condition numbers. It shows regression curves that do or do not visibly overfit across polynomial degree or basis count. No test or held-out error is ever measured, so no risk curve exists to show a fall-rise-fall shape. The introduction mentions benign generalisation of rich models and cites Belkin et al. only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is correct. The authors conclude that regularisation does not solve overfitting in regression. Well-conditioned problems can overfit yet must not be regularised, and an ill-conditioned problem needs regularisation despite little overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses polynomial and exponential-basis least-squares regression examples to examine overfitting and regularisation; it does not implement the double-descent measurement in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that the extent of overfitting depends on the interval of the independent variable, comparing Examples 4 and 5. It also contrasts polynomial and exponential-basis examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Example 3 (16 points, degree up to 20): curves do not visibly overfit for 3≤d≤12 but do for large d, including past the interpolation point, while the effective condition number falls to about 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In polynomial least-squares regression, visible overfitting past the interpolation point can coexist with a well-conditioned problem where ridge regularisation is inappropriate.

fits_no_version.finding: Degree-22 polynomial fits of Runge-type functions on 13 points overfit at the interval tails, with or without noise. The extent depends on the interval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterised polynomial fits show Runge-type oscillatory overfitting whose extent depends on the data interval.

fits_no_version.finding: Exponential-basis fits of 26 points: n=7 shows no overfitting; n=30 (overparameterised, ill-conditioned) shows small overfitting, much less than the polynomial cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overfitting past interpolation depends on the basis family, not only on parameter count.

record.peer_reviewed: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
record.problems: The examples do not report test error or evaluate double-descent curves. Several curve-overfitting outcomes are described qualitatively or shown in figures; no uncertainty estimates or controls are reported for these outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. Condition estimates, singular-value diagnostics, and regularisation-method comparisons are not outcomes for the listed double-descent versions.

untested.parts: No test-error sweep over model size; no deep networks.
No variation of sample count with measured test error.
Polynomial and exponential-basis regressions sweep capacity through interpolation (d=15 in Ex. 3, d=12 in Ex. 4, n=26 in Ex. 6), but only curve shapes are shown, not risk.
No effective-complexity measure used to predict an error peak; the effective condition number concerns numerical stability, not generalisation.
Noise is added at SNR 7 or 25 and regularisation is discussed, but no error peak is measured against noise or tuned regularisation.
No re-indexing of a risk curve by effective parameters.

record.verdict_notes: Overfitting is judged visually from plotted curves; no train/test split or error metric is reported. The sweeps cross the interpolation point, but no double-descent risk curve can be read from them. The paper is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size or interpolation threshold.
No test-error measurement over training epochs or time.
No comparison of test error across training-sample counts near interpolation.
No risk curve across capacity for any model class.
No test of a shared effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations.
No double-descent peak analysis by noise or regularisation, and no test for triple or multiple descent.
No comparison of a double-descent curve with a curve indexed by effective parameter count.
